topic: Can human memory be stored, manipulated, and transplanted digitally?

research_brief.object: Task-defined episodic memories represented across distributed neural states and digital latent models
research_brief.central_hypothesis: A digital representation that preserves a target memory at fidelity level k reconstructs target content and relations under held-out cues, remains distinct from nuisance and non-target states, and shows selective causal sensitivity when manipulated.
research_brief.boundary: No human or animal memory has been uploaded, edited, or transplanted by this design artifact.

fidelity_ladder.name: predictive_access
fidelity_ladder.criterion: predict recall or item identity on held-out trials

fidelity_ladder.name: behavioral_association
fidelity_ladder.criterion: produce target-related response in constrained task

fidelity_ladder.name: neural_reinstatement
fidelity_ladder.criterion: reproduce target-specific neural state under held-out cues

fidelity_ladder.name: content_preserving_reconstruction
fidelity_ladder.criterion: recover content, temporal order, and relations with bounded errors

fidelity_ladder.name: transfer_or_recollection
fidelity_ladder.criterion: recipient passes neural, behavioral, and independent content tests

stages.name: Data contract and memory task
inputs: approved de-identified human data or approved animal engram data

stages.name: Causal validation and promotion
stages.criterion: selective target effect beyond sham and non-specific disruption with independent content validation

unknowns: which memory features generalize across contexts
whether digital representation preserves content identity after transfer
whether manipulation can be selective without collateral effects
how subjective recollection can be independently validated
human_review_required: animal welfare if engram work is pursued
statistical review of content scoring and leakage
